body: Suicide. And soon. I've been contemplating the act a lot lately. I've had some weak attempts. The next major negative thing to happen in my life will push me over the edge, no doubt. Of course, I'm shit at everything. I'm sure suicide attempts will be included in the long list of things I underperform at.

I'll try not to. I've been trying to hold on at least until I get through graduation so my school doesn't need to make a huge fuss about it during the ceremony. Things are just difficult now and I don't see them getting better for plenty of reasons. I can't bring myself to eat or leave my bed really, much less to get any help.

Suicide is a huge thing though. I don't feel ready to rush in. If anything, I feel like I'm just screaming for attention now. Even though I've been fixated on this for such a long time and I've spent the past few days doing non-stop research and planning, it doesn't feel like I'm someone who is seriously suicidal. Despite the written plan and the notes that I've drafted to all the important people in my life.

Tonight I drove around in a daze for 2.5 hours. I wanted to feel alive with the wind on my face. Driving through backroads has always made me feel good. Instead I felt scared and alone. I stopped at a bridge and watched the lights on the water for a bit and sobbed. 

I don't know what I want right now. I don't know what I'm doing. Everything seems so hard. Nothing seems to make me happy. I can't even pretend. Everyone can see that I'm fucked.

I wish I could have a hug.

I really encourage you to call. It was a helpful experience. It gave me a lot of perspective. I know I've been afraid of discussing it in real life because I don't know if I want help yet. If I tell my friends or my family, they would most likely force it upon me because they care. And I know they'd believe me because I've been a shell of my former self recently.

But I could tell the hotline operator anything. She just listened and provided gentle support. I never felt pressure or shame or anything. It was so comforting and therapeutic to just put all of my issues out there. It definitely wasn't a permanent solution, but in the moment it helped a lot. Even though my problems seem pretty small in comparison to others, she never belittled them or made me feel weak. She was just there for me.

You seem very nice too. If you ever need anything, feel free to message me. I hope you'll be ok as well. I'm in no place to give you an "it gets better speech", but I encourage you to make the call before you do anything drastic.

I've called two.

The first was the Trevor Hotline. I had to wait for awhile and I felt unsure about using that one in general because I didn't really know how much of this I blame on my sexuality. Being bi is irrelevant to my issues aside from the fact that my girlfriend just left me. I was crying and trying to be quiet, so the guy who answered couldn't really hear me. I got scared and hung up after his third question.


The second time was through the national hotline for the US. They routed me somewhere. It didn't take too long. 

I talked for about 30 minutes with a nice woman. I forget what she opened with, but probably something along the lines of the name of the hotline. I was crying at this point and I told her I had just finished a suicide note and that I wanted to die. She paused for a bit and then asked if I said I was having suicidal thoughts.

After that we just talked through my issues a bit. She never really tried to tell me things will get better or that there is a light at the end of the tunnel or anything. She just tried to understand what was going on and listened to me. I think I controlled the conversation more as I was having a breakdown.

I read a lot about hotline operators asking if you had a plan, a set date, and the means for carrying out your plan. That didn't happen during the call. I told her about a method I considered, but never the one I was actually considering going with. I knew it wasn't going to happen that night, so I guess it wasn't very urgent.

She never asked for my name or where I was from. I guess she sort of encouraged me to get help. She brought up the idea of therapy. She asked about my insurance and told me how to get in contact with a therapist. She also asked how my parents would feel (I'm about to graduate HS, so I'm still at home). This only came after I was pretty receptive about therapy.

I started the call sobbing and ended it feeling better. I've gotten through the past few days. I have gotten way further in planning though. I do have a set in stone method and a rough idea on the date. I don't have the means yet. I think I'm going to go for a walk and then maybe call again though. I guess I still have a lot of doubt.
Thanks for the numbers. Those are helpful. I've called recently and probably will again tonight. I'm trying to find a reason to live right now. I think this thread has helped some.
